policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv מחצצרים and qere מַחְצְרִים are spelling variants of the same hiphil participle 'sounding trumpets'; ASV 'the priests sounded trumpets' renders either identically, no italic supply bears on it, and the verse's only note (alternative_rendering, 'for the song of Jehovah') concerns a different phrase and cannot decide a reading. Base qere fallback retained.
